messages:
Ellen P.: dropped a compact mock for the alerting panel focusing on stacked channels + quiet-hours: https://www.figma.com/file/compact-alerts. Main question: can users parse thresholds, ordering, and suppression state at a glance when space is tight? Ravi M.: quick scan 3: love the density. concern: tiny tooltips contain the only numeric details (threshold %, evaluation window). tooltips == inaccessible. prefer inline microchips like \"CRIT · 90% · 5m\" that remain visible in compact mode. Keisha B.: agree. also the preview \"+3\" overflow loses routing semantics. proposal: show the next 2 channels and a labeled overflow chip: \"+3 (2 suppressed)\". that communicates both count and suppression. a11y-bot: auto-check: issues found: 1) 3.4:1 contrast on microchips (fail) 2) preview updates lack aria-live role=\"status\" 3) drag handles not keyboard focusable. recommendations: increase contrast to 4.5:1 for small text, add
Preview...
, and provide tabindex=0 for handles with visible focus ring. Ellen P.: noted. I'll update chips and add role=status. microcopy question: current label reads \"Silence window\"; I'm leaning to \"Quiet hours (suppression window)\" to help non-ops users. thumbs? Ravi M.: +1 to combined label. keyboard flow nit: tab order should reach Preview before channel actions so the aria-live announcement is heard immediately after edits. right now preview is below the list and skipped by tabbing. Keisha B.: visual idea: a tiny timeline pill in preview showing quiet-hours range with a striped pattern for suppressed segments (good for colorblind). fallback text: \"Suppressed 12:00 AM6:00 local\". Also add a timezone toggle (Local / UTC) next to the pill. Ellen P.: will mock timeline pill + timezone toggle. also adding an undo snackbar anchored to preview when thresholds change: \"Threshold set to 85% 5s Undo\" so keyboard users can dismiss. a11y-bot: extra note: ensure snackbar has role=\"alert\" and keyboard focusable undo button. provide aria-live polite for the change, and role=alert for the undo so assistive tech notices it immediately. Sam (PM): please try to get a clickable prototype with inline chips, overflow label, timeline pill, timezone toggle, and undo toast by next Tue. we'll schedule 4 quick feedback sessions with SREs + support. Ellen P.: will iterate and post v2. thanks all. :thumbsup:
